source.title: Scaling Properties for Artificial Neural Network Models of a Small Nervous System
source.authors: Quilee Simeon; Leandro Venâncio; M. Skuhersky; Aran Nayebi; Ed Boyden; G. Yang

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling experiments to self-supervised prediction of C. elegans neural activity, a setting beyond text pretraining, and reports data- and model-size results.
record.gate_note: The paper reports neural-activity prediction loss scaling, architecture comparisons, and source-specific data-scaling curves. It cites the original language-model scaling papers, but those citations are not treated as results. Synthetic-dataset results are not extracted because the 60-row limit is used for the real-data scaling strata and the model-size comparison.
record.test_reason: The study trains ANN models on self-supervised next-timestep prediction of C. elegans neural activity, a modality outside text. It reports validation-MSE scaling against training data (1 to 284 worms, fitted slopes -0.40 to -0.65) and against parameter count. That bears directly on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. More precisely: MSE decreases log-linearly with data, with slopes that depend on architecture but not on data source. MSE is non-linear in model size, and recurrent models do best (only they beat the naive baseline). The authors say the data trend suggests collecting more recordings is a fruitful near-term route, though long-horizon prediction is not yet achieved.
record.recipe_differences: Uses self-supervised next-timestep prediction of C. elegans neural activity and validation MSE, rather than language-model pretraining and held-out cross-entropy; the work is an extension to biological neural dynamics.
record.method_sensitivity: Scaling behavior depends on model architecture; the authors report similar data-scaling slopes across the different experimental data sources.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched ~580K parameters, the data-scaling slope depends on architecture class (CTRNN -0.65, FF -0.40) but not on the experimental data source.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-scaling exponents depend on architecture inductive bias but are stable across data sources within a domain.

record.code_released: not stated (the paper names the GitHub repository metaconsciousgroup/worm-graph)
record.problems: The paper reports MSE rather than cross-entropy and does not fit or report power-law exponents or prediction errors for extrapolations. Numerical outcomes are largely presented in figures; uncertainty estimates are not stated in the provided text. Model-size behavior is described as nonlinear, and only the CTRNN and LSTM beat the naive predictor.
record.rows_left_out: Synthetic-dataset scaling results in Fig. 6A-D were not extracted; the 60-row limit was used for the real-data architecture-by-source curves and real-data model-size outcomes. Those omitted figures describe Sines and Random Walk data-scaling and model-scaling experiments.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss is measured.
No fit-then-predict test on larger runs. The abstract says data scaling 'extrapolates', but no extrapolation is checked.
No fixed-compute sweep or compute-optimal allocation.
Only different architecture classes are compared at ~580K parameters. Depth, width or shape within a class is never varied (the core is fixed at a single layer).
No downstream tasks; Fig. 7 autoregressive generation is qualitative only.
No comparison of fitting choices, parameter counting or schedules.
No compute scaling. Data range is only ~2.5 orders of magnitude (1–284 worms). No fitted model-size exponent.

missing.what: Synthetic-data scaling: Sines shows sequence models beating baseline beyond a data/size threshold; Random Walk shows no model beating baseline. Model hidden size was swept over [8, 4096].
Per-model minimum validation losses and parameter counts; Linear minimum 0.03533 vs baseline 0.03541.

record.verdict_notes: The negative slopes (-0.40, -0.65) on MSE around 0.035 only make sense on log-log axes, so this is a power law in data, but over only ~2.5 orders of magnitude and without uncertainty estimates. The 48 source-specific rows all rest on one aggregate statement about similar slopes. The DOI is an IEEE SoutheastCon 2024 paper; the text is the bioRxiv preprint version. The record's 'preprint' status may therefore be wrong.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses neural-activity prediction MSE, not held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy, and does not test scaling in language models.
It does not fit laws on small runs and assess predictions of much larger runs.
It does not sweep a fixed compute budget or estimate compute-optimal parameter and token allocations.
It compares different model classes at approximately matched parameter count, but does not isolate depth, width, or other architecture changes within one model class over a wide range.
It tests neural-activity prediction, not image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer. It does not establish a fitted power-law form across multiple orders of magnitude.
It varies architecture and data source, but does not compare fitting choices, parameter-counting conventions, or training schedules as causes of differing fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits.

relationships.condition: Data scaling at a fixed ~580K parameters on real C. elegans neural-activity prediction, mixed data, evaluated on the pooled set and on each of 8 source validation sets
relationships.reason: Validation MSE falls log-linearly with training timesteps, with slopes -0.40 (FF) to -0.65 (CTRNN). Slopes are similar across sources. Rows D-MIX-*, D-KATO-* to D-LEIFER-*.
relationships.display_finding: Validation MSE fell log-linearly with training timesteps, with slopes from −0.40 for feedforward networks to −0.65 for continuous-time recurrent networks and similar slopes across sources.

relationships.condition: Model-size scaling on the full real dataset D_ALL
relationships.reason: MSE is 'a nonlinear function' of model size, varies by architecture, and no power law is fitted; only recurrent models beat the naive baseline. Rows M-SIZE-*.
relationships.display_finding: MSE varied nonlinearly with size and architecture, and only recurrent models beat the naive baseline.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Approximately parameter-matched architecture classes in the mixed-dataset scaling experiment and source-specific evaluations
reader_labels.reason: Architecture affects the reported data-scaling behavior: CTRNN and Feedforward have different stated slopes, and the authors describe architecture as influential; rows D-MIX-FF, D-MIX-CTRNN, and D-KATO-FF through D-LEIFER-LINEAR.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Real C. elegans neural-activity prediction as training-data amount increases
reader_labels.reason: Validation MSE decreases with more training data; the paper describes a monotonic log-linear reduction and reports similar slopes across experimental sources, rows D-MIX-FF through D-MIX-LINEAR and D-KATO-FF through D-LEIFER-LINEAR.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Model-size scaling on real C. elegans neural-activity prediction
reader_labels.reason: The reported model-size relationship is nonlinear and varies by architecture; only CTRNN and LSTM beat the naive-predictor loss, and the study does not fit or validate a common power law, rows M-SIZE-FF through M-SIZE-ATTENTION.
